Cyber Attack Disrupts Operations at Finnish Renewable Energy Firms

HELSINKI, June 7 – A cyber attack targeting Finnish renewable energy companies has disrupted operations across several wind and solar power facilities, industry officials said Friday. The incident, which began late Thursday, involved ransomware that locked critical IT systems at multiple firms, causing production slowdowns and some sites to halt output entirely.

Northern Sky Renewables, one of the affected companies, confirmed that its Turku wind park had been “safely taken offline” as a precaution. “We are working closely with authorities to restore systems and ensure the safety of our facilities,” said company spokesperson Liisa Karvonen. “Our priority is the wellbeing of our staff and the integrity of our operations.”

The Finnish Renewable Energy Association stated that at least five companies have reported significant IT disruptions, with dozens of employees unable to access operational platforms or reporting tools. “This is an unprecedented event for our sector in Finland,” said the association’s director, Jari Mäkelä. “Our members are focused on maintaining safety and minimizing impact while investigations continue.”

Some solar installations in Central Finland have also reduced power generation due to the loss of remote monitoring capabilities. On-site workers have been deployed to affected locations to oversee manual operations, but several sites remain partially or fully offline.

The National Cyber Security Centre has confirmed it is investigating the attack, which is ongoing as of Friday evening. “We urge all renewable energy operators to review their cyber defenses and remain vigilant,” a spokesperson said.

Authorities have not disclosed who may be behind the attack. No injuries to personnel have been reported.
